item.title: Ottolenghi on Simple Food in Complicated Times
item.description: Israeli-British chef Yotam Ottolenghi joins Mishal Husain to discuss challenges facing the hospitality industry, the politics of food and the Israeli elections in a conversation recorded live in London. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Egypt Court Orders Closure of Prominent Independent News Website
item.description: A Cairo court ordered the closure of Mada Masr, one of Egypt’s few remaining independent news outlets, and fined its editor-in-chief for operating it without a license.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Roknifard: 47 Years of Hostility Means No US-Iran Trust
item.description: Oil rose higher on the back of a Wall Street Journal report which says the US told several Gulf countries to be prepared for a short, intense military campaign after the midterm elections. This comes amid a regional diplomatic push to avert a fresh round of fighting in the Persian Gulf. Julia Roknifard, Senior Lecturer School of Law & Governance at Taylor's University, Malaysia spoke to Bloomberg’s Abeer Abu Omar on Horizons Middle East & Africa. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Can Andy Burnham's UK Budget Help Shopping Town Centers, High Street Retailers?
item.description: The prime minister has vowed to save struggling town centers. The budget is the first test of his radical plan.
item.dc:creator: Maddie Parker and Sabah Meddings

item.title: Israel Election Is in Deadlock as Netanyahu, Eisenkot Blocs Stay Neck and Neck
item.description: Israel’s election has so far delivered an electoral cliffhanger, with Benjamin Netanyahu and Gadi Eisenkot’s blocs short of the 61 seats needed for a parliamentary majority. Bloomberg's Dan Williams breaks down what this means and what could be next. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Canada CEOs Are Warming to Carney’s Economic Policy, Survey Finds
item.description: One of Canada’s most influential business groups says its members are warming to Prime Minister Mark Carney’s more interventionist economic agenda, and they largely support his plans to diversify exports and boost investment.
item.dc:creator: Erik Hertzberg

item.title: Putin Courts Africa Leaders at Moscow Summit to Expand Influence
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin will host dozens of African leaders in Moscow as the Kremlin seeks to deepen ties with a continent that has taken on greater strategic importance for Russia since its 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Prabowo to Meet Singapore Envoy on Mission to Ease Relations
item.description: Indonesia President Prabowo Subianto will meet Singapore’s top diplomat on Wednesday as ties between the two Southeast Asian nations come under strain.
item.dc:creator: Norman Harsono

item.title: Mbappé China Backlash Prompts China’s Warning for Global Celebrities
item.description: The official newspaper of China’s ruling Communist Party warned that global celebrities risk losing their commercial appeal in the country if they offend local audiences, as widening backlash against French football star Kylian Mbappé puts his brand partnerships under pressure.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Israeli Vote Too Close to Call Between Netanyahu and Eisenkot
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot are neck and neck in the country’s first election since the 2023 Hamas attacks, setting up a tense period of negotiations over who will form the next government.
item.dc:creator: Marissa Newman, Dan Williams, Shira Rubin and Alisa Odenheimer

item.title: Bolsonaro Reportedly Arrives Miami Amid Investigations
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro arrived in Miami after fleeing Brazil following a defeat in its presidential election, according to O Globo. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Israeli Arab Parties Claim Kingmaker Status in Extra-Tight Vote
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu spent much of election day warning his base that Arab citizens were voting in record numbers. He was right.
item.dc:creator: Shira Rubin

item.title: Judge Questions DOJ Bid to Set Aside 20,000 California Votes
item.description: A US judge in Los Angeles expressed skepticism about a Trump administration attempt to block California from counting 20,000 mail-in ballots from people the federal government claims are likely non-citizens registered to vote in the upcoming midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Erik Larson

item.title: Bolsonaro Arrives in Miami After Fleeing Brazil, O Globo Says
item.description: Brazilian senator Flávio Bolsonaro arrived in Miami on Tuesday after fleeing his country following a defeat in its presidential election, O Globo reported.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Carvalho and Eric Martin

item.title: US to Issue Visas to Flavio Bolsonaro and His Family
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Michael Oren, former Israeli ambassador to the US, says many Israelis are in shock as Gadi Eisenkot's bloc holds a narrow lead over Benjamin Netanyahu's, but cautions that the result could still change as votes are counted. Rep. Greg Landsman (D-OH) says more voters are casting ballots early and that the numbers suggest a strong night for Democrats in Ohio, while cautioning there are still seven days until Election Day. Rep. Darrell Issa (R-CA) says redistricting could backfire in some states by creating more competitive seats that require significant campaign spending. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Xi’s Corruption Purges Upend Hunt for China’s Next Top Leaders
item.description: As hundreds of China’s top politicians gather in Beijing this week, President Xi Jinping is facing a problem of his own making: His sweeping purges are draining the pipeline he needs to staff senior roles next term.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Rep. Issa Says Redistricting Creates More Seats in Play
item.description: Rep. Darrell Issa (R-CA) says redistricting could backfire in some states by creating more competitive seats that require significant campaign spending. Issa says Flavio Bolsonaro's departure from Brazil could help settle questions around the country's transition of power, while cautioning that his presence in the US does not necessarily mean he will be allowed to conduct political activity from here. On Israel, Issa says Netanyahu would likely continue an aggressive approach toward Iran, Gaza and southern Lebanon if he remains prime minister during another election cycle. Issa also says Congress should address the debt ceiling during the lame-duck session and expects lawmakers to pass the defense authorization bill on a broadly bipartisan basis. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Says High Gas Price a ‘Short-Term Pain’ at Texas Rally
item.description: President Donald Trump returned to Texas on Tuesday in a final attempt to bolster Senate candidate Ken Paxton, whose close race in a normally reliable conservative state has Republicans worried about losing control of the chamber.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason

item.title: Israeli Vote Deadlocked With Netanyahu Level With Opposition
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot are neck and neck in the first election since the 2023 Hamas attacks, setting up a tense period of negotiations over who will form the next government.
item.dc:creator: Shira Rubin, Galit Altstein and Ethan Bronner

item.title: Johannesburg’s Infrastructure Crisis Puts South Africa’s Investment at Risk
item.description: Power cuts, water shortages and crumbling roads are undermining Johannesburg’s economy and threatening its ability to retain businesses and attract investment. Can South Africa’s City of Gold turn itself around? On this episode of Next Africa, Jennifer Zabasajja examines the financial pressures and political instability behind Johannesburg’s decline, and whether upcoming local elections could help change its course. Business Leadership South Africa CEO Busi Mavuso explains why companies are being forced to work around failing public services. Ninety One founder and CEO Hendrik du Toit discusses the investment needed to rebuild the city, while Eskom CEO Dan Marokane explains how the utility moved from rolling blackouts to excess generating capacity—and why Johannesburg still faces outages. Plus, Bloomberg South Africa Bureau Chief Alex Parker assesses the city’s infrastructure backlog and prospects for recovery. (Source: Bloomberg)
